Disease of gums and tooth-supporting periodontal tissues; these belong to the gastrointestinal axis.

Epilepsy defined by an underlying metabolic abnormality; both neurologic disease and metabolic mechanism apply.

Endocrine lesions, characteristic skin lesions and cardiac myxomas are major diagnostic features; cardiac myxoma reported in 6/11.
Inherited cardiac repolarization disorder causing QT prolongation and ventricular arrhythmias; syncope does not establish neurologic damage.

Severe developmental brain disorder; skeletal defects 6/6, sensorineural hearing loss 5/5, cardiac defects 6/8. Oral anomalies, including cleft palate 3/6, omitted at cap.
Distal arthrogryposis defines congenital joint contractures; supplied ancestry also identifies a congenital nervous system disorder.
Nipple carcinoma is a breast primary; epithelial histology alone does not establish a separate skin primary.
Hodgkin lymphoma arising in the spleen; splenic and lymphoid disease is haematologic, and lymphoma requires the immune mechanism axis.
Immune-mediated intestinal inflammation; extraintestinal diseases are separately diagnosed or do not consistently reach 30% across this umbrella.

Destructive fungal infection; sinusitis and cutaneous infection each occur in 30-79%. Ocular, CNS and gastrointestinal manifestations are occasional (5-29%).
Immune-mediated post-injury pericarditis; pleuritis/pleural effusion commonly accompanies it (~50% or more) and forms part of syndrome criteria.

Carcinoma of the uterine corpus; reproductive organs have no designated axis.
Variola minor causes a characteristic destructive vesiculopustular skin eruption, potentially leaving scars.
B-cell lymphoma occupying the stomach; gastrointestinal origin, lymphoid-cell neoplasia and lymphoma mechanism determine the axes.
Carcinoma arising in the supraglottic larynx; the larynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
